summary.value: Radio used to select multiple options.

a11y.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.rule: Ensure enough spacing around each radio button so it is easy to select, including on touch devices
value.quote: Make sure there is enough spacing around each radio button so that it is easy to select, including on touch devices.

value.rule: Avoid placing radio buttons next to each other, as it makes them harder to read and problematic for users who need to zoom
value.quote: Avoid placing radio buttons next to each other. This makes them harder to read and creates problems for users who need to zoom a webpage or app to see clearly.

value.rule: Avoid disabled states if possible due to low colour contrast
value.quote: Avoid disabled states if possible. They have low colour contrast, which can be problematic for some users.

value.rule: Disabled radios cannot meet contrast requirements without causing confusion about interactivity
value.quote: disabled cannot meet contrast requirements, because if the contrast were higher, users might think the element is active, try to select it, and not understand why nothing happens.

value.rule: Radio uses arrow keys (not Tab) to move between options within a group
value.quote: Note that we use the arrow keys to select options in the Radio component, not the Tab key.

value.rule: A group of radio options should always have a legend and option labels
value.quote: A group with multiple options should always have a legend and option labels .

value.rule: In horizontal layouts, it must be clear which text belongs to which button
value.quote: When using a horizontal layout, it must be clear which text belongs to which button.

relations.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.note: Use checkbox instead of radio when the user should be able to choose more than one option
value.quote: Avoid radio when the user should be able to choose more than one option, use checkbox instead

value.note: Use fieldset to group multiple radio choices together
value.quote: Use fieldset for grouping multiple choices.

value.note: Consider suggestion instead of radio when users need more choices than a radio group comfortably supports
value.quote: If users need more choices, consider using suggestion or select .

value.note: Consider select instead of radio when users need more choices than a radio group comfortably supports
value.quote: If users need more choices, consider using suggestion or select .

value.note: A switch may be more suitable than radio when there is only a single choice to make
value.quote: If there is only one choice to make, a switch or a checkbox may be more suitable.

composition.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.rule: There should not be more than seven options in one radio group
value.quote: There should not be more than seven options in one group.

value.rule: Sort options alphabetically unless there is a clear reason not to
value.quote: Sort options alphabetically unless there is a clear reason not to.

value.rule: Be careful about placing the most common option first when the question is personal or value-based
value.quote: Be careful about placing the most common option first if the question is personal or value-based, such as sexual orientation or political affiliation.

value.rule: Place radio buttons vertically whenever possible to make the list easier to scan and read
value.quote: Place radio buttons vertically whenever possible. This makes the list easier to scan and the options easier to read.

value.rule: Horizontal layout is acceptable only for two short-label options or rating scales
value.quote: You can use a horizontal layout when there are only two options with short labels, such as “Yes” and “No”, or in a rating scale ranging from “strongly disagree” to “strongly agree”.

value.rule: Radio can be positioned horizontally with flex, but should generally be placed vertically
value.quote: Radio can be positioned horizontally with flex , but should generally be placed vertically .

value.rule: Consider whether a preselected option is appropriate for the context
value.quote: Consider whether a preselected option is appropriate for the context.

value.rule: A preselected option can influence informed choice and may be perceived as manipulative or discriminatory
value.quote: A preselected option can influence the user's ability to make an informed choice, and some users may experience it as manipulative or discriminatory.

value.rule: Place a description meant to inform the choice directly after the legend
value.quote: When the description is intended to help users understand the question and provide necessary information before they make a choice, it should be placed directly after the legend.

value.rule: Answer options should be as short as possible and follow the same linguistic form
value.quote: Answer options should be as short as possible, and each option should follow the same linguistic form.

value.rule: An error message for an unanswered required group should apply to the entire group of options
value.quote: If the user attempts to continue without answering a required question, the error message should apply to the entire group of options.

value.rule: For a valid form element, use ds-field together with a label
value.quote: For a valid form element, we recommend using <ds-field> together with a <label> .

value.rule: Radio is a composite component built from field, label, validation message, and input
value.quote: Radio is a composite component that uses field , label , validation message , and input to create a radio.
